subject: Meteorology
title: ENIAC and the First Computer Forecast
description: A fast breakdown of ENIAC and the First Computer Forecast for builders.

hook.text: In 1950, a team led by Jule Charney used the ENIAC computer to produce the first successful numerical weather forecast.

buildup.text: ENIAC occupied an entire room—30 tons of vacuum tubes and wiring, yet slower than a modern pocket calculator.

discovery.text: The forecast took 24 hours to compute a 24-hour prediction—barely fast enough to be useful, but it worked.

twist.text: Richardson's dream from 1922 was finally realized—physics equations could predict weather when computed fast enough.

climax.text: This breakthrough launched operational numerical weather prediction—by the late 1950s, computers made daily forecasts.

punchline.text: A room-sized computer, one day to compute one day—and NWP was born.

quiz.question: How long did ENIAC take to produce its first 24-hour weather forecast?
